title: Certificate-Guided Pruning for Stochastic Lipschitz Optimization
claim: Points whose optimistic upper envelope falls below the best certified lower bound are provably suboptimal and can be pruned, leaving a shrinking candidate region.
layout: Single panel, 1-D plot, left-to-right, shaded active region with brace label
description: A single 1-D toy plot with f(x) on the vertical axis and x on the horizontal axis. A red curve U_t(x), the Lipschitz upper envelope, undulates across the plot with two dips on the left and right and a hump in the middle. A green dashed horizontal line marks the global lower bound ℓ_t. A grey dashed curve shows the unknown true function f(x), which lies below the envelope. Blue dots with error bars show noisy samples and their confidence intervals. The central region, where the red envelope is above the green line, is shaded light orange and braced below as A_t (active set). The flanking regions, where the envelope is below the line, are labeled 'pruned' in grey. The eye goes first to the orange block and the red envelope crossing the green line.
caption: The active set At (shaded) consists of points where the Lipschitz envelope Ut(x) (red) exceeds the global lower bound ℓt (green dashed). Regions where Ut(x) < ℓt are certifiably suboptimal and pruned, causing At to shrink as sampling proceeds.
abstract: We study black-box optimization of Lipschitz functions under noisy evaluations. Existing adaptive discretization methods implicitly avoid suboptimal regions but do not provide explicit certificates of optimality or measurable progress guarantees. We introduce \textbf{Certificate-Guided Pruning (CGP)}, which maintains an explicit \emph{active set} $A_t$ of potentially optimal points via confidence-adjusted Lipschitz envelopes. Any point outside $A_t$ is certifiably suboptimal with high probability, and under a margin condition with near-optimality dimension $Î±$, we prove $\Vol(A_t)$ shrinks at a controlled rate yielding sample complexity $\tildeO(\varepsilon^{-(2+Î±)})$. We develop three extensions: CGP-Adaptive learns $L$ online with $O(\log T)$ overhead; CGP-TR scales to $d > 50$ via trust regions with local certificates; and CGP-Hybrid switches to GP refinement when local smoothness is detected. Experiments on 12 benchmarks ($d \in [2, 100]$) show CGP variants match or exceed strong baselines while providing principled stopping criteria via certificate volume.
